key_insight: A small cross-tissue RNA splicing signature can act as a quantitative biomarker for ReNU syndrome, strongly distinguishing pathogenic RNU4-2 T-loop variants from controls.
clinical_relevance: This biomarker could support preclinical and clinical development of therapies for ReNU syndrome by providing a reproducible readout of disease severity and treatment response.
method: Analyzed RNA-seq data from two independent cohorts of people with ReNU syndrome and controls.
Focused on shared alternative splicing events, especially alternative 5 splice-site (A5SS) changes.
Derived a minimal 6-site splicing signature and tested it in blood and iPSC-derived neuron-like cells.
evidence_signal: Across 30 ReNU syndrome cases and 54 controls, the 6-site signature perfectly separated 19 n.64_65insT cases from controls and produced no false positives in 5,984 additional whole-blood controls.
watch_item: The signature appears specific to T-loop variants, so it may not generalize equally to all RNU4-2 variant classes or all sample types.
paper_title: A cross-tissue splicing signature as a quantitative biomarker for ReNU syndrome
